close_reason: Aggregated all six cross-field 'at least one of' constraints (Name/Organization/SpeakToAs/OnlineService/Address/Author) into a single rustdoc table in the crate-level docs, and added a corresponding README §Gotchas bullet. Kit posture preserved — no validate() helper or breaking type-system change; the aggregation makes the consumer-side validation surface explicit. Commit 650bc95.
description:
Six public structs in lib.rs document a cross-field at-least-one-of
constraint in their type-level rustdoc, then leave each component
field individually Option (or otherwise unenforceable at the type
level). A caller constructing the struct with all the listed fields
set to None has no compile-time or runtime signal that the resulting
value is spec-non-conformant.

The struct list with the documented constraint:

- Name (lib.rs:92-93): \"At least one of [components] or [full]
  must be set per the RFC; this is not enforced at the type level.\"
- Organization (lib.rs:204-205): \"At least one of [name] or [units]
  must be set per the RFC; this is not enforced at the type level.\"
- SpeakToAs (lib.rs:268-269): \"At least one of [grammatical_gender]
  or [pronouns] must be set per the RFC.\"
- OnlineService (lib.rs:397-398): \"At least one of [uri] or [user]
  must be set per the RFC; this is not enforced at the type level.\"
- Address (lib.rs:603-605): \"At least one of components, coordinates,
  country_code, full, or time_zone must be set per the RFC; this
  is not enforced at the type level.\"
- Author (lib.rs:1145-1146): \"At least one property other than @type
  must be set per the RFC; this is not enforced at the type level.\"

This is the cross-field counterpart of sgrr.17 (which catalogs
single-field mandatory-as-Option cases on Resource-derived types).
Filed separately because the failure mode differs: sgrr.17 callers
can defend with a per-field is_some() check; cross-field callers
must implement an or-of-is_some chain per struct, and the chain
differs across the six struct shapes. The defensive code every
consumer writes:

    fn ensure_name_valid(n: &Name) -> Result<(), MissingName> {
        if n.components.is_none() && n.full.is_none() {
            return Err(MissingName);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    fn ensure_org_valid(o: &Organization) -> Result<(), MissingOrg> {
        if o.name.is_none() && o.units.is_none() {
            return Err(MissingOrg);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    // ... four more, one per struct ...

Three ways to address (callers cannot enforce these constraints
without writing six wrapper functions):

(a) Wrap each affected field group in an enum representing the
    valid combinations. Example for Name:

        pub enum NameValue {
            Components(Vec<NameComponent>),
            Full(String),
            Both { components: Vec<NameComponent>, full: String },
        }

    Pushes the invariant into the type system. Breaking change.

(b) Add a fallible validate() method to each affected struct that
    returns Result<(), TypeError>. Non-breaking but optional —
    callers can still skip it. The kit currently has no precedent
    for validate() helpers, so introducing the pattern would be
    a workspace-wide policy decision.

(c) Document the constraint in lib.rs:16-23 (\"Design: optional
    fields and Option<...>\") so a contributor reading the doc-
    comment on partial-response Option modelling knows the
    cross-field constraints are a separate axis of unenforced
    invariants. Pair with a README §Gotchas note enumerating the
    six structs and the constraint shape for each.

Recommendation: (c). The kit's posture is \"types model the wire
shape; semantic validity is the consumer's job\" (per the kit-vs-jig
section in workspace AGENTS.md). Enforcing cross-field constraints
in the type system would diverge from that posture and force the
partial-response Option modelling into a corner. The realistic
mitigation is documentation: tell the caller they MUST validate
before emitting and give them the per-struct constraints to check.

Filed at P3 because the constraints are already documented at the
type level — they're just not enforced. Caller has the information
needed; what they lack is a single place to find all of them.

Related: sgrr.17 (single-field mandatory-as-Option). The fix for
this finding does not depend on sgrr.17's outcome — the failure
modes and remediations are independent.
title: Cross-field 'at least one of X, Y' constraints documented but not enforced on 6 structs
